newsitem.title: SWEDEN: SWEDISH SHARES END HIGHER BOOSTED BY FORESTRY.
newsitem.headline: SWEDISH SHARES END HIGHER BOOSTED BY FORESTRY.

text.p: Swedish shares closed higher on Tuesday with forestry shares leading the upward trend and the market boosted by the stronger dollar.
The Stockholm general index rose 0.63 percent to 3,266.80 after fairly active trade worth 5.50 billion crowns.
"New York's the only possible worry," said one broker.
The forestry sector posted the largest gains with the sector index rising 3.03 percent after rising on Wall Street.
Swedish player AssiDoman rose seven to 240 crowns after posting a six month profit after financial items of 859 million crowns against market expectations of 819.
Its profit a year ago was 1.23 billion crowns.
Fellow forestry company SCA is due to release its six month results on Wednesday. It rose five to 196 crowns, benefitting from the positive sentiment in the sector.
S-E-Banken, the first of Sweden's big four banks reported for the half year, but disappointed the market with a lower than expected profit showing depressed margins.
S-E-Banken posted a six month operating profit of 2.86 billion crowns against expectations of 3.02 billion crowns. Its share price fell 2.50 to 96 crowns.
Specialty toolmaker Sandvik released its result.
It posted an 18 percent lower profit after financial items of 2.11 billion crowns against market expectations of 2.17 billion crowns with mixed sales across different units.
"It was in line with expectations, maybe a bit on the low side, which reflected a different mix," CI Nordic Securities analyst Peter Karlsson told Reuters.
Its share ended 3.5 crowns higher at 261 but off the day's high of 265 crowns.
Swedish Match edged up 0.5 to 24.70 crowns. It posted a 33 percent rise in pre-tax profit for the first half to 758 million crowns. -- Stockholm newsroom +46-8-700 1017
